key_findings.story: Long context win signal confirmed across qa1 16k+32k AND qa2 16k. vanilla 100% gibberish at 16k+ on all 3 tasks; mem_space 15-20% retrieval

note.surprise_finding: qa5/8k mem_space partial 85% > Beacon-Qwen2-7B 63%. Why: chunked path generates verbose 'According to the text, X gave Y to Z' answers that contain target entity name as substring. qa5 targets are person/item names (single words) so substring match liberal. qa1 targets are location words (also liberal). qa2 needs multi-fact reasoning so verbose answers often miss correct target.
note.implication: previous qa1/8k=39% 'failure' is partly substring-match strictness on chunked verbose output, not real semantic failure. Need lenient match (any candidate location word) for fair comparison.

note.story_update: qa5/32k mem_space 30%p vs vanilla 0%p → +30% win extension to 32k. qa2 vanilla 0-4k filled in: 44/41/47/44%. Vanilla < Beacon by 13-23% on qa2 short context (8B-Inst weaker than Qwen2-7B-Inst on multi-fact). Our mem_space ≈ vanilla on qa2 0-4k (small loss)

note.discovery: qa5/8k mem_space=86 > vanilla=72p → +14 win on QA5 8k against own vanilla, not just vs Beacon

note.key_insight: strict substring match was over-counting qa5 because 'Fred', 'apple', 'milk', 'kitchen' etc are short tokens that frequently appear in verbose chunked-path output regardless of correct answer. Lenient (first-candidate-in-output) is more honest. qa5 strict 86/67/44 → lenient 31/22/21. Win still holds but more realistic.
